nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a single-tape machine over a finite inhabited alphabet and $w$ a word over that alphabet. The fenced machine of $M$ halts on the fenced input of $w$ with $i$ padding cells on the left and $j$ on the right for some $i, j \in \mathbb{N}$ if and only if $M$ halts on $w$.
nodes.title: The fenced machine halts on some padding of a word iff the machine halts on it

nodes.summary: There exist a finite inhabited alphabet $\Gamma$ with a primitive recursive encoding, a linear bounded automaton $F$ over the fenced alphabet of $\Gamma$, and a primitive recursive map $e$ from codes of partial recursive functions to words over $\Gamma$, such that the set of codes $c$ for which $F$ halts on none of the fenced inputs of $e(c)$, with $i$ padding cells on the left and $j$ on the right for any…
nodes.title: Emptiness of a linear bounded automaton on computable input slices is undecidable

nodes.summary: For a word $w$ over an alphabet $\Sigma$ and $i, j \in \mathbb{N}$, the fenced input of $w$ with $i$ padding cells on the left and $j$ on the right is the word over the fenced alphabet of $\Sigma$ made of a wall, $i$ left padding cells, the letters of $w$ as symbols, $j$ right padding cells and a wall, in this order.
nodes.title: Fenced input

nodes.summary: A transition of a single-tape machine $M$, made of an optional symbol to write, an optional move and an optional next state, becomes the transition of the fenced machine of $M$ that writes the symbol, or a right padding cell where $M$ writes a blank, makes the same move, and goes to the running state of the next state $q$ of $M$, or halts where $M$ halts.
nodes.title: A transition lifted to the fenced machine

nodes.summary: In the running state of a state $q$ of a single-tape machine $M$, the fenced machine of $M$ acts on the cell under its head as follows: on a symbol $a$ it makes the lifted transition of $M$ in state $q$ on $a$; on a left or right padding cell it makes the lifted transition of $M$ in state $q$ on a blank; on a wall or a blank cell it leaves the cell unchanged, does not move, and enters the trap.
nodes.title: The running transition of the fenced machine

nodes.summary: For a set of states $Q$, the states of the fenced machine are two start states, a running state for each state $q \in Q$ of the simulated machine, and a trap state.
nodes.title: States of the fenced machine

nodes.summary: For an alphabet $\Sigma$, the tape alphabet of the fenced machine consists of a symbol for each letter of $\Sigma$, two kinds of padding cells (left and right), which the simulated machine reads as blanks, and the wall, which marks the ends of the input.
nodes.title: Fenced alphabet

nodes.summary: For a single-tape machine $M$ over a finite inhabited alphabet $\Sigma$, the fenced machine of $M$ is the single-tape machine over the fenced alphabet of $\Sigma$ whose states are the states of the fenced machine for the states of $M$, which starts in the first start state and acts on the cell under its head as follows. In the first start state, on a wall it moves right into the second start state, and on any other…
nodes.title: The fenced machine

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a single-tape machine over a finite inhabited alphabet and $w$ a word over that alphabet. The fenced machine of $M$ halts on none of the fenced inputs of $w$, with $i$ padding cells on the left and $j$ on the right for $i, j \in \mathbb{N}$, if and only if $M$ does not halt on $w$.
nodes.title: The fenced machine halts on no padding of a word iff the machine does not halt on it

nodes.summary: Let $w$ be a word of length $\ell$ and $i, j, n \in \mathbb{N}$. The cell at position $n$, counting from $0$, of the fenced input of $w$ with $i$ left and $j$ right padding cells is the wall if $n = 0$; a left padding cell if $1 \le n \le i$; the letter of $w$ at position $n - i - 1$, also counting from $0$, as a symbol, if $i < n \le i + \ell$; a right padding cell if $i + \ell < n \le i + \ell + j$; the wall if…
nodes.title: Cells of a fenced input

nodes.summary: For every single-tape Turing machine $M$, the fenced machine of $M$ is a linear bounded automaton.
nodes.title: The fenced machine is a linear bounded automaton

nodes.summary: For a word $w$ of length $n$ and natural numbers $i$ and $j$, the fenced input of $w$ with $i$ padding cells on the left and $j$ on the right has length $i + n + j + 2$: the word, the two paddings and the two walls.
nodes.title: Length of a fenced input

nodes.summary: For every cell $o$ of the simulated machine, a symbol or a blank, the fenced cell of $o$ is not a wall.
nodes.title: A fenced cell of a write is never a wall

nodes.summary: For a cell $o$ of the simulated machine, a symbol or a blank, the fenced cell of $o$ is the cell the fenced machine writes for a write of $o$: $o$ itself if $o$ is a symbol, and the padding cell $\mathrm{pad}$ if $o$ is a blank.
nodes.title: Fenced cell of a write

nodes.summary: Let $o$ be a cell of the simulated machine, a symbol or a blank, and copy it to the fenced machine, a symbol as itself and a blank as a blank. Then the simulated cell of the copy is $o$.
nodes.title: Reading back a copied cell

nodes.summary: For every cell $o$ of the simulated machine, a symbol or a blank, the simulated cell of the fenced cell of $o$ is $o$.
nodes.title: Reading back a fenced cell of a write

nodes.summary: The simulated cell of a cell of the fenced machine is the cell of the simulated machine that it stands for: a symbol of the simulated machine stands for itself, and every other cell (a padding cell, a wall or a blank) stands for a blank.
nodes.title: Simulated cell of a fenced cell

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
